body:
### Summary

The lock command fails to pick up any dependencies declared in the `project.dependencies` field of the `pyproject.toml`.

The issue seems to only affect one of my projects, and it began without any changes to my pyproject.toml or workflow in-general.

For context: I have been iterating on another repo so I had one of my dependencies' sources set to the branch of a git repo I'm working on. Every time I pushed changes to the branch of the other repository I ran `uv lock -P <dep2> && skaffold build`. For weeks this was working without issue. Until yesterday (9/17/26) when it no longer saw `<dep2>` and removed it as well as all of the corresponding transitive dependencies from my lock file.

I tried clearing cache, as well as adding a public dependency like PyTorch to the project dependencies via `uv add` and although `torch` was added to `project.dependencies` neither it nor its transitives made it into the lock file.

However, when I add the same dependencies into the `dependency-groups` table everything works correctly.

---

Here is a sample of the offending `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
dynamic = ["version"]
name = "repo"
description = "A python based image."
readme = "README.md"
license = "Dummy License"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
keywords = []
requires-python = ">=3.13"
authors = []
maintainers = []
dependencies = ["dep1", "dep2"]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://<private-gitlab>/repo"
Repository = "https://<private-gitlab>/repo.git"
Issues = "https://<private-gitlab>/repo/-/issues"
Changelog = "https://<private-gitlab>/repo/-/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.version]
path = "VERSION"
pattern = "(?P<version>[^']+)"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/repo"]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "PRIVATE"
url = "https://<private-gitlab>/api/v4/groups/00000/-/packages/pypi/simple"
default = true

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "httpx[cli]>=0.27.2",
  "pytest>=8.3.3",
  "pytest-asyncio>=1.1.0",
  "pytest-mock>=3.14.1",
  "python-levenshtein>=0.27.1",
  "pytest-benchmark",
  "pylint>=4.0.6",
]
```
